note: What ARM's own documentation says this silicon IS. Where the documents are silent, conformance/suites.json names what answers instead and what that is worth. When an implementation disagrees with this file, the implementation is wrong, no matter how widely used it is.

documentsNote: Four documents, one of which decides. Only the ARM60 datasheet gives this part cycle by cycle; the other three are cited where they say something it does not.

order: the ARM60 datasheet, for anything it prints: the instruction set, the programmer's model, the memory interface, and chapter 10's per-instruction per-cycle bus behaviour
ARM DDI 0004D, the ARM610 datasheet, as a second witness for the instruction set and the programmer's model, never for a timing
ARM Application Note 11, for the 26-bit mode encodings the datasheets do not tabulate, and for what an unobserved restriction does
ARM DDI 0100E, the Architecture Reference Manual, for instruction-level behaviour the datasheets leave unstated and it states for architecture version 3
the filtered SingleStepTests ARM7TDMI corpus, state only, for instruction-level behaviour no document specifies
authority.why: The first three are the manufacturer's, and among them the ARM60 datasheet is the only one describing this part's bus. The corpus is a recording from an implementation of a later part, so it is a good source for behaviour nobody wrote down and a poor one for anything a manufacturer printed. Where the two disagree the document wins. ARM DDI 0020C and ARM DDI 0024C are deliberately absent: they are ARMv3 and they disagree with ARM6 in three rows of the speed table, so they are witnesses that the timings differ rather than witnesses to what they are.

comparedAgainst.what: The ARM-state files of SingleStepTests/ARM7TDMI, pinned by commit in conformance/suites.json and filtered per that file, compared on processor state alone. Its cycle and transaction data is never read: ARM60's multiply worst case is 1S+16I and the ARM7TDMI's is 1S+4I, so the transaction stream belongs to a different part's bus.

authority.notMeasured: Nothing here rests on a measurement of real silicon. No ARM60 has been probed for this package and no FPGA implementation of this architecture is known to exist, so rungs two and three of the family ladder are empty and say so.

parts.summary: The ARM60 as its own datasheet describes it, configured for a 32 bit program and data space, which is what chapter 9 recommends and what the rest of that document describes.

addressBus.quote: ARM60 has a 32 bit address bus, unlike earlier ARM processors which had a 26 bit address bus.

staticImplementation.quote: ARM60 is a fully static CMOS implementation of the ARM which allows the clock to be stopped in any part of the cycle with extremely low residual power consumption and no loss of state.

registerCount.quote: The processor has a total of 37 registers made up of 31 general purpose 32 bit registers and 6 status registers.

r15Read.quote: When R15 is read, bits [1:0] are zero and bits [31:2] contain the PC.

modesAvailable.quote: When using a 32 bit program space there are a total of 10 modes available.

reservedBits.quote: Only eleven bits of the PSR are defined in ARM60

multiplierRadix.quote: The multiply and multiply-accumulate instructions use a 2 bit Booth's algorithm to perform integer multiplication.

multiplyRdEqualsRm.quote: A MUL will give a zero result if Rm=Rd, and a MLA will give a meaningless result.

multiplyCarry.quote: the C flag is set to a meaningless value

multiplyEarlyTermination.quote: The multiplier is shifted right 2 bits per cycle, and when it is zero the instruction terminates

multiplyWorstCase.quote: The maximum time taken by any multiply is therefore

resetOverwrites.quote: Overwrites R14_svc and SPSR_svc by copying the current values of the PC and CPSR into them.

resetUndefined.quote: The value of the saved PC and CPSR is not defined.

resetForcesMode.quote: Forces M[4:0]=%10011 (Supervisor mode) and sets the I and F bits in the CPSR

resetCost.quote: Nreset must remain LOW (and Nwait must remain HIGH) for at least two clock cycles, and during the LOW period the processor will perform dummy instruction fetches with the address incrementing from the point where reset was activated.

interruptLatency.quote: The total time is therefore 28 processor cycles.
interruptLatency.unreachable: The 28 cycles include a three-cycle input synchroniser and a data abort entry, and the model has neither a synchroniser nor an abort input to take one.

cycleTypesPipelined.quote: In the following tables Nmreq and seq (which are pipelined up to one cycle ahead of the cycle to which they apply) are shown in the cycle in which they appear, so they predict the address of the next cycle.

stretchingAccessTimes.quote: there is no limit upon the maximum period for which mclk may be stretched, or Nwait held LOW.

nwaitTiedHigh.quote: If Nwait is not used in a system, it may be tied HIGH.

mclkPhases.quote: The clock may be stretched indefinitely in either phase to allow access to slow peripherals or memory.
mclkPhases.unreachable: The model has no mclk phases: a cycle is one indivisible step, and how long it lasts is the caller's Waits rather than anything the part holds.

noMinimumClock.quote: ARM60 is a static design and there is no minimum clock speed.

storedCounter.quote: the stored value will be address of the instruction plus 12

prefetchOffset.quote: If the shift amount is specified in the instruction, the PC will be 8 bytes ahead. If a register is used to specify the shift amount the PC will be 12 bytes ahead.

emptyRegisterList.quote: The only restriction is that the register list should not be empty.

lockDuringSwap.quote: It is active only during the data swap (SWP) instruction.

coprocessorAbsent.quote: it must not drive cpa or cpb LOW. These will remain HIGH, causing the undefined instruction trap to be taken.

undefinedNotTrapping.quote: some instruction codes are not defined but do not cause the Undefined instruction trap to be taken
undefinedNotTrapping.section: 7.14 Instruction Set Summary, note beneath Figure 28

conditionNotMet.quote: Any instruction whose condition code is not met will fail to execute. It will add one cycle to the execution time of the code segment in which it is embedded

neverCondition.quote: The never (NV) class of condition codes shall not be used as they will be redefined in future variants of the ARM architecture.

teqp.quote: its effect is to move SPSR_<mode> to CPSR if the processor is in a privileged mode and to do nothing if in User mode.
teqp.section: 7.3.6 The TEQ, TST, CMP and CMN opcodes

unalignedLoad.quote: an address offset from a word boundary will cause the data to be rotated into the register so that the addressed byte occupies bits 0 to 7

endianness.quote: ARM processors which do not have selectable Endianism (ARM2, ARM2aS, ARM3, ARM61) are Little Endian.

lateAbort.quote: When it is HIGH (Late Abort) the modified base register of an aborted LDR or STR instruction is written back.
lateAbort.unreachable: No memory system here can refuse an access, so the abort pin is never driven and no LDR or STR is ever aborted for lateabt to decide about.

provisionalFigures.quote: The timing parameters given here are preliminary data and subject to change when device characterisation is complete.
provisionalFigures.unreachable: Chapter 12's AC parameters are analogue timings of the pins, and the model keeps no time, so none of its figures enters anything it computes.

seqDefinition.quote: will become HIGH when the address of the next memory cycle will be related to that of the last memory access. The new address will either be the same as or 4 greater than the old one.

nopcDefinition.quote: When LOW this signal indicates that the processor is fetching an instruction from memory; when HIGH data (if anything) is being transferred.

exceptionEntry.quote: Exceptions (and software interrupts) force the PC to a particular value and refill the instruction pipeline from there.

shiftBitSeven.quote: Note that the zero in bit 7 of an instruction with a register controlled shift is compulsory; a one in this bit will cause the instruction to be a multiply or undefined instruction.

lslZero.quote: Note that LSL #0 is a special case, where the shifter carry out is the old value of the CPSR C flag.

lsrZero.quote: The form of the shift field which might be expected to correspond to LSR #0 is used to encode LSR #32, which has a zero result with bit 31 of Rm as the carry output.

rrx.quote: rotate right extended (RRX). This is a rotate right by one bit position of the 33 bit quantity formed by appending the CPSR C flag to the most significant end of the contents of Rm

registerShiftByte.quote: Only the least significant byte of the contents of Rs is used to determine the shift amount.

logicalFlags.quote: the C flag will be set to the carry out from the barrel shifter (or preserved when the shift operation is LSL #0), the Z flag will be set if and only if the result is all zeros

arithmeticFlags.quote: The C flag will be set to the carry out of bit 31 of the ALU, the Z flag will be set if and only if the result was zero

immediateRotate.quote: The immediate value is zero extended to 32 bits, and then subject to a rotate right by twice the value in the rotate field.

immediateRotateCarry.quote: If the rotate immediate is zero, the carry-out from the shifter is the value of the C flag, otherwise, it is set to bit[31] of the value of <shifter_operand>.
immediateRotateCarry.section: A5.1.3 Data-processing operands - Immediate, Architecture version: All
immediateRotateCarry.why: ARM60 section 7.3.3 gives the rotate and stops, while section 7.3.1 says a logical operation takes its C flag from the shifter. This is the sentence that says what that flag is.

branchOffset.quote: Branch instructions contain a signed 2's complement 24 bit offset. This is shifted left two bits, sign extended to 32 bits, and added to the PC.

branchPrefetch.quote: The branch offset must take account of the prefetch operation, which causes the PC to be 2 words (8 bytes) ahead of the current instruction.

writingR15.quote: When Rd is R15 and the S flag is set the result of the operation is placed in R15 and the SPSR corresponding to the current mode is moved to the CPSR.

blockTransferOrder.quote: The registers are transferred in the order lowest to highest, so R15 (if in the list) will always be transferred last. The lowest register also gets transferred to/from the lowest memory address.

unalignedLoadBigEndian.quote: An address offset of 0 or 2 from a word boundary will cause the data to be rotated into the register so that the addressed byte occupies bits 31 through 24.

wordStoreUnaffected.quote: The word presented to the data bus is not affected if the address is not word aligned.

postIndexedRmEqualsRn.section: 7.6.5 Restriction on the use of base register

r15AsBase.quote: When using R15 as the base register one must remember that it contains an address 8 bytes on from the address of the current instruction.

byteLoadZeroFilledBigEndian.quote: The selected byte is placed in the bottom 8 bits of the destination register and the remaining bits of the register are filled with zeros.

abortDuringBlockLoad.quote: All register overwriting is prevented after the Abort is indicated
abortDuringBlockLoad.unreachable: No memory system here can refuse an access, so the abort pin is never driven and no block load is ever aborted part way through.

swapIsLocked.quote: implemented as a memory read followed by a memory write which are

modeBitsOnlyDescribed.quote: Not all combinations of the mode bits define a valid processor mode. Only those explicitly described shall be used.

reservedBitsPreserved.quote: Unused bits in the PSRs are reserved and their state shall be preserved when changing the flag or control bits.

modes26bit.quote: There are a total of ten operating modes in two overlapping sets.
modes26bit.why: ARM60 Table 1 prints the six 32-bit encodings and no more, and ARM610 Table 2 is identical to it. The four 26-bit encodings appear in no datasheet found; Application Note 11 Table 1 is where they are printed, and the ARM60 datasheet names that note by title.

arm2asFallback.quote: In all cases, if these restrictions are not observed, the behaviour of the processor is the same as that of the ARM2aS macrocell. However there is no guarantee that future ARM processors will behave in the same way.
arm2asFallback.why: This is why every 'shall not be used' in the ARM60 datasheet has an answer somewhere, and why that answer is not this part's own document. It is also why the published corpus is not evidence about those corners: the part it was recorded from is one of the future processors the sentence declines to guarantee.

coreIsTheArm6.quote: The CPU within ARM610 is the ARM6.
coreIsTheArm6.why: Recorded because it is the reason the catalogue could grow and the reason it has not. The instruction set carries across ARM60, ARM600 and ARM610; the bus does not, and only ARM60 has a document that gives it cycle by cycle.
